products.title: Metric Male 74° Cone Hose Fitting
products.descriptionShort: Metric Male 74° Cone — metric thread with a 74° included cone seat (37° per side), in 19 sizes from -02. Not interchangeable with the metric 60° cone.
products.descriptionLong:
The Metric Male 74° Cone Hose Fitting is the male half — a metric thread with the cone machined on the fitting of the metric 74° cone range — a hydraulic hose fitting with a metric thread and a 74° included cone seat, sealing metal-to-metal against the mating cone.

What the 74° seat is

74° is the included angle — 37° per side, the same seat geometry the JIC 37° flare uses. The seat is the only thing the two share: this fitting carries a metric thread, so it will not mate with a JIC port and a JIC fitting will not mate with this one. If the port you are facing is metric and the seat is a cone rather than a flat face or an O-ring groove, measure the cone before ordering — the metric 60° cone in this same category looks near-identical and does not seal against a 74° mating half.

Construction

  • Configuration: straight
  • Thread form: Metric (M10×1 to M45×2)
  • Sealing form: 74° included cone seat (37° per side), metal-to-metal
  • Gender: male
  • Material: carbon steel, zinc-plated and Cr3+ passivated (316 stainless on request)

Sizes

19 sizes, hose bore -02 to -20, threads M10×1 to M45×2. The full size and dimension table is on this page.

How to order

Quote the Indus part number for the size you need. Tell us the hose grade and bore and we will include the matching crimp ferrule — the ferrule follows the hose, not the fitting. Indus crimps and pressure-tests assemblies before dispatch.

faqs.question: How is this different from a JIC 37° fitting?
faqs.answer: The seat is the same — 74° included, 37° per side — and the thread is not. This fitting is metric; JIC is UN/UNF. They will not screw together. If your port is metric and the seat is a cone, this is the family you want; if the thread is inch, use the JIC range.

faqs.question: How is this different from the metric 60° cone in the same category?
faqs.answer: Only the cone angle, and it matters. A 74° male will not seal against a 60° female — the two cones touch on a line instead of a face and the joint weeps under pressure. Both use metric threads of the same nominal sizes, so the thread will happily start. Measure the cone, not the thread.

faqs.question: What thread sizes are available?
faqs.answer: Metric (M10×1 to M45×2). The table on this page lists every thread against every hose bore, including the fine-pitch variants where the catalogue carries both — M12×1.25 and M12×1.5 are separate part numbers, not the same fitting.

faqs.question: What sizes are available?
faqs.answer: 19 sizes, hose bore -02 to -20. Every combination in the table is an orderable part number.

faqs.question: What is the maximum working pressure?
faqs.answer: The hose grade and bore set the assembly rating, not the fitting. A correctly crimped fitting does not derate the hose. Tell us the grade and bore on the RFQ and we will confirm the figure in writing.

faqs.question: Which ferrule pairs with this fitting?
faqs.answer: The one that matches your hose grade — the skive/no-skive choice follows the hose construction, not the fitting end. Send the hose grade with your enquiry and we will specify the ferrule and the crimp diameter.

faqs.question: Is stainless steel available?
faqs.answer: Yes — 316 stainless on request across the range, for marine, offshore and washdown service. Standard supply is carbon steel, zinc-plated and Cr3+ passivated. Add "-SS" to the part number when you enquire.

faqs.question: Can Indus crimp the assembly?
faqs.answer: Yes. We crimp, pressure-test and certify assemblies in Dubai and ship UAE-wide. Send the hose grade, bore, both end fittings, overall length and orientation.

specs.label: Applicable Standards
specs.value: Metric thread to ISO 261 (coarse and fine pitch)
